title: Do you have any trick to make Claude a better 3D animator?
author: Codingology
selftext:
I need to make very short animations like idle, walking, turning around, sleeping etc.  
Unfortunately I know nothing about animating in blender, never went inside that world.  
Opus 5.5 high does a relatively robotic job and the results aren’t very natural. Maybe it is because my models are not human like but animal like.

Do you have any skill or something to make it do a better job?

comments.author: 328amdev
comments.body: For animal movement, I’d start with a reference clip of the closest real animal and work on one walk cycle first. Give it the rig’s bone names and specific targets, like keeping each foot planted during contact and shifting the body’s weight over the supporting legs. Get that working before adding tail or ear motion. Could you share a short clip of the current result?

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body:
There is a free bandai namco motion dataset which can be worth checking out.

[https://github.com/BandaiNamcoResearchInc/Bandai-Namco-Research-Motiondataset](https://github.com/BandaiNamcoResearchInc/Bandai-Namco-Research-Motiondataset)

replies.author: CampaignReboot
replies.body: https://www.mixamo.com/ is also a good resource

comments.author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
comments.body:
People will tell you that you need the blender MCP but Opus animations are still primitive and robotic.

You need argon and give it blender access. Argon does like a math matrix of the entire physics in your game and is able to do any animation you want and look fluid.

replies.author: Late-Oven-9575
replies.body: Where I can use argon to connect blender?

replies.author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
replies.body:
You'll need the $100 gemini plan (or above) as that's the only plan that allows Argon to work with your files locally. You'll then download AntiGravity desktop app, which is Googles version of Claude and ChatGPT desktop.

There you just connect your project files and blender MCP plugin and ask it away.

I initially signed for one month to help with ThreeJS animations, and I've only been using it for animations but the results are so fluid and insane. It usually one-shots most animations.

replies.author: thecrustycrap
replies.body: Interesting, thanks for sharing🙏, but damn $100 is a lil out of budget, will see if there are alternatives

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: I have claude for all models to rows of all animations from multiple directions from beginning to end, its like 64 images or something,. It draws the bones and a gizmo to show xyz direction, and uses filters to check the first and last frame to see if they are the same, amoung other passes.  its not perfect but I've gotten decent horse and sheep animations

comments.author: PrestigiousAppeal743
comments.body: There are pretty small models specifically for 3d animation you can run in comfy UI... Originally id generate the animations from a text prompt, import them to my model in blender, and adjust them in the graph editor. Now I just tell Claude to do all that for me... It comes up with a prompt and goes from there, better than if I do it manually.

comments.author: SeaweedOk9985
comments.body:
I think people have access to AI but are scared to actually use it in what I believe to be the better way.

Ask claude:

Create a prompt for the purpose of designing a script that will take a video of a person. Then using computer vision finds, stabalises their skeleton and then uses the motion of that person to create an animation that can be used in blender by mapping the motion to the skeleton of the model in blender. It needs to be smooth and realistic.

You'll end up with something you can just pass videos of you doing those actions.

Get creative. Having LLMs doesn't mean an agent should do literally everything. instead use it to make creating these things easier. The benefit is that an LLM doesn't have to struggle with interpreting your idea of what you want the animation to look like.

comments.author: mirageofstars
comments.body: Right but you mentioned Argon before?

comments.author: s22stumarket
comments.body:
I have tried several video to mocap softwares. The best one and the one I now only use is Uthana. I has an API so Claude can directly upload videos there. Even the manual upload is the best UX wise and results are great. No hand motion though.

And I actually filmed over 150 animations of myself to populate the "idle", filler and background character animation pools.

comments.author: DigitalDustChan
comments.body: There are plenty of animations for sale, and it's really not hard to take a professionally made animation and modify it slightly for the specific body you are working with. So just buy it. You don't have to pay all your money to the giant AI companies, some of it can go to creators.
